sum: NAVER (NHNCF) shares fell 5.12% to 172,500 won at the November 13 regular-session close in Seoul, extending a slide that began after weak quarterly profit. The Korean search and internet group is tied to Nvidia through a recent $1 billion equity investment, according toInvesting.com, so Jensen Huang's resignation landed close to home.

The earnings backdrop was already shaky. Third-quarter revenue rose 10.7% to a record 3.472 trillion won, but operating profit fell 20.9% to 451.3 billion won and net profit dropped 45.2% to 402.5 billion won. The sharp drop in operating profit stemmed from higher spending on AI infrastructure. The top traders appear to have continued buying NAVER on the dip for a second session, taking advantage of the lower share price.

The stock jumped during its trading debut but ended the day at 9,890 won, about 20% below its offering price of 12,400 won. FTC launches review of Naver Financial-Dunamu deal
sum: The Korea Fair Trade Commission (FTC) has begun deliberations on the proposed merger between Naver Financial Corp., South Korea’s largest online payment provider, and Dunamu Inc., operator of Upbit, the country’s largest cryptocurrency exchange.

The FTC said Tuesday it had submitted its merger review report to the commission and sent it to the companies Friday. The report outlines potential legal violations identified by FTC examiners and their proposed corrective measures. Its submission marks the start of formal deliberations on the deal.
Under the proposed transaction, Naver Financial would acquire all of Dunamu’s shares, making it a wholly owned subsidiary, in exchange for around 2.54 Naver Financial shares for each Dunamu share.
The FTC received the merger filing in November last year, a year before submitting its review report.

FTC examiners identified 10 markets in which the merger could affect competition, including online payments, digital asset exchanges, search portals, online advertising, online shopping and unlisted stock brokerage services.
The review also covers the potential impact on a domestic market for Korean won-denominated stablecoins, which has yet to be established.

The FTC said it considered the possibility that the merger could affect future competition in the market, citing a maturing regulatory environment, with more than 10 digital asset-related bills introduced in the National Assembly.

South Korea recommends conditional approval of Naver Financial’s deal with Dunamu — Korea Herald
sum: South Korea’s antitrust regulator has moved to the final stage of reviewing the acquisition of Dunamu, which operates the Upbit cryptocurrency exchange, by payment services operator Naver Financial. The secretariat of the Fair Trade Commission submitted a report for consideration by the agency’s full commission and recommended conditionally approving the deal after assessing the companies’ updated commitments, Korea Herald reports.

The deal could combine the country’s largest online payments provider and its largest cryptocurrency exchange, creating a digital financial platform valued at approximately 20 trillion won, or $14.9 billion. The full commission must decide whether to approve the transaction, impose conditions on it, or block it. A decision is expected by the end of the year, nearly a year after the companies submitted their application for approval.

Under the terms of the proposed share-swap transaction, Dunamu shareholders are to receive approximately 2.54 Naver Financial shares for each Dunamu share. Once the deal is completed, Dunamu will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Naver Financial.

The Fair Trade Commission believes the transaction could restrict competition in digital finance markets. The review covered 10 potentially affected segments, including online payments, cryptocurrency exchanges, search, online shopping, and financial data services.

The regulator analyzed 12 instances of overlap or interaction between the companies’ businesses and identified competitive risks in 10 of them. At the same time, direct overlap in stock investment platforms and online marketplaces for used goods is unlikely to significantly restrict competition, according to the agency.

The review also concerned the not-yet-formed market for won-denominated stablecoins, although there is currently no regulatory framework for their issuance in the country. Jeong Seong-bok, a representative of the regulator, said that a bill on such stablecoins has already been introduced and that entering this market is identified as a priority in the companies’ documents.

The assessment identified four potential sources of adverse effects on competition, including links between stablecoin issuance and cryptocurrency trading, as well as between cryptocurrency trading and online payments.

Nvidia Completes $1 Billion Investment in Naver for 4.13% Stake
sum: Nvidia completed a $1 billion investment in South Korean internet company Naver on Nov. 6, receiving a 4.13% stake as the companies advance an artificial intelligence infrastructure partnership announced in June.

Naver raised about $1 billion through a private placement of more than 6.5 million shares. The share sale generated about 1.3 trillion South Korean won in proceeds and gave Nvidia its stake through a third-party allotment.

The investment is expected to accelerate the companies' AI factory project, part of a partnership announced in June. Naver plans to begin the project at its Gak Sejong data center in Sejong, where it will build GPU-based infrastructure.

The company also plans to expand its GPU-as-a-Service business, linking that service to the project's planned infrastructure. The data center will serve as the starting point for the effort, which combines a facility buildout with a service expansion. The deal adds an equity investment to Nvidia's AI infrastructure activity in Asia.

(Yonhap Interview) New Italian trade commissioner sees K-food as gateway to broader bilateral trade
sum: SEOUL, Nov. 7 (Yonhap) -- The new commissioner at the Seoul office of the Italian Trade Agency (ITA) said K-food could help open the door to broader trade ties between South Korea and Italy, particularly in the wine sector.

"We plan to focus more on the wine sector, which is such an important part of Italian culture," Raimondo Lucariello said in a recent interview with Yonhap News Agency on Thursday, as the ITA marks the 100th anniversary of its founding.

Praising the popularity of Korean food globally and the country's vibrant cuisine scene, Lucariello said the agency plans to offer more wine-tasting classes tailored to South Koreans, whom he described as "great drinkers of soju," referring to the country's traditional distilled liquor.
He also pointed to the global popularity of Korean movies and music, saying Italy has much to learn from South Korea's success in promoting its cultural content internationally.
The ITA is a public agency tasked with supporting Italian companies in expanding their presence in overseas markets and promoting Italian products and businesses abroad.
High Street Italia, the agency's permanent Made in Italy promotional showroom and lifestyle complex located in southern Seoul, is a key part of such efforts.
It is the only showroom of its kind operated by the ITA worldwide, except for a similar yet smaller facility in Taipei opened just two months ago.

South Korea's KOSPI Plunges More Than 5% for Second Day, but Kakao and Naver Surge Around 10% as Money Rotates Into Platforms and Biotech
sum: Even in a rout that sent South Korea's KOSPI down more than 5% for a second consecutive session, buying piled into non-semiconductor sectors such as platforms, biotech and automakers, producing stocks with double-digit gains. As the semiconductor and AI infrastructure value chain took a direct hit from U.S.-driven regulatory worries, money rotated into sectors that had been overlooked.

An analysis of Korea Exchange data on Nov. 6 showed that of the 805 common stocks traded on the main board the previous day, when the KOSPI fell 5.28%, 302 (37.5%) closed higher. Decliners numbered 475 (59.0%), with 28 (3.5%) unchanged. That means that despite the index's sharp drop, a considerable number of individual stocks rose.

Platform stocks drew the most attention. Kakao climbed 10.65% and Naver gained 8.26%. Foreign investors net bought 71.4 billion won (approximately $52.6 million) worth of Naver, making it the top foreign net-buy that day, while institutions bought 54.3 billion won (approximately $40.0 million) worth. Kakao also saw foreign and institutional net buying of 26.6 billion won (approximately $19.6 million) and 19.6 billion won (approximately $14.4 million), respectively. The buying appears to be money that exited semiconductor stocks and flowed into platform names.

For Kakao, the announcement of shareholder return measures and third-quarter results served as catalysts. Kakao's board met the previous day and filed a corrected disclosure of its spin-off plan, adjusting the schedule and ratio. Under the revised plan, an extraordinary shareholders' meeting to approve the split will be held on Jan. 15 next year, and the spin-off date is set for Feb. 1, 2027. Third-quarter revenue was 2.0867 trillion won (approximately $1.5 billion) and operating profit was 240.3 billion won (approximately $176.9 million), up 6.3% and 7.4% respectively from a year earlier, in line with market expectations.

Institutional money also flowed into large pharmaceutical and biotech names. Celltrion rose 7.50%, with trading value of 428 billion won (approximately $315.0 million), the highest among gainers. Institutions net bought 223.3 billion won (approximately $164.4 million) worth of Celltrion, their second-largest purchase after SK Hynix.

sum: SEOUL, Nov. 5 (Yonhap) -- The South Korean won nudged lower against the U.S. dollar Thursday, as offshore investors remained net sellers of local stocks after a Democratic Party win in the U.S. midterm elections.
The won was quoted at 1,342.1 won per dollar at 3:30 p.m., down 0.6 won from the close of the previous stock trading session.

With Democrats winning majorities in both the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives, traders have expected it to weaken the power of U.S. President Donald Trump during the final two years of his term.
For the local semiconductor industry, one of the key things to watch going forward is whether a Democrat-controlled Congress would slow the pace of building data centers for artificial intelligence.

Foreign investors sold a net 3.39 trillion won (US$2.53 billion) worth of local shares during the latest regular stock trading session, with the benchmark Korea Composite Stock Price Index plunging 5.28 percent to close at 5,383.80.

Siemens stock gains as Naver talks spotlight industrial AI
sum: Siemens stock traded at 268.08 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 10:35 CET on Monday, November 2, 0.91 percent above the Xetra close of Friday, October 30. The move came as fresh industrial AI discussions added a strategic technology angle ahead of Siemens' next corporate update.

The Herald Business reported on Monday that Siemens Group Chairman Roland Busch and Naver CEO Choi Soo-yeon held a dialogue on industrial AI at the Asia-Pacific German Business Conference in Seoul on Saturday, October 31. The talks focused on combining German engineering with Asian strengths in AI, chips and digital platforms across manufacturing, energy and mobility.

Choi said industrial AI would reach a true tipping point only when small and midsize companies and their suppliers could use it with ease. She also stressed that human oversight becomes more important as AI handles a wider range of tasks. The comments frame adoption as a supply-chain and productivity issue rather than only a software feature.

Busch said industrial AI would create its full value only when deployed safely and reliably in the field and scaled across industries. That emphasis is relevant for Siemens because the group's industrial offering combines automation, software and digital-twin capabilities with applications in physical production environments.

After the dialogue, Siemens executives visited Naver's 1784 headquarters. The companies discussed cases in which Naver's digital-twin technology has been used in industrial settings and explored ways to take those applications into global markets alongside Siemens' industrial solutions. They also considered cooperation involving robotics and robot foundation models.

The discussions build on a June memorandum of understanding between Naver Cloud and Korea Siemens to advance AI transformation in manufacturing. The planned cooperation combines Siemens industrial automation and digital-twin technology with Naver Cloud's AI and cloud infrastructure, while also targeting joint customer development and industry-specific projects.
For investors, the talks reinforce Siemens' positioning in industrial AI but do not by themselves establish additional revenue or earnings.

Naver shares in freefall as Nvidia investment fails to lift stock
sum: Naver's share price has been plunging to historic lows even as positive news continues to emerge. When Nvidia's $1 billion investment in the company was confirmed Friday, the stock still tumbled to 165,000 won during trading — a sign that even major good news cannot arrest the decline.
After the announcement, Naver shares rose 4.13 percent in after-hours trading Saturday, but fell even further when regular trading resumed.
Naver said Nvidia will invest $1 billion in the company on Friday, becoming its third-largest shareholder.

Earlier, Naver signed a new share subscription agreement with Nvidia on July 24 and decided to issue new shares through a third-party allotment. At the time, Nvidia set a condition requiring Naver to secure at least $9 billion worth of computing infrastructure for AI factory expansion, separate from the $1 billion investment. Naver recently signed a related agreement with Brookfield, satisfying that prerequisite.
"Much of the concern that had been raised about whether Naver's business would proceed will be substantially resolved," said Ahn Jae-min, an analyst at NH Investment & Securities.

Shareholders who had hoped the confirmed Nvidia investment would lift the stock were left stunned. The share price, which had topped 300,000 won earlier this year, has collapsed to near historic lows. Many investors are said to have bought Naver shares at peak prices between 280,000 and 300,000 won, leaving a significant number sitting on losses of roughly 50 percent.
"I thought the share price would go up, but it fell even further," one Naver shareholder said.

Google Chrome Logs 260 Million Hours to Lead Naver in Korea
sum: Google Chrome logged 260 million hours of mobile usage in South Korea in September, extending its lead over local portal Naver for the fifth consecutive month.
Chrome held the top spot after outpacing Naver’s 240 million hours during the month, according to mobile app analytics firm Wiseapp Retail.

Samsung Internet took third place with 130 million hours. Together, the top three applications generated 630 million hours, accounting for about 80 percent of total usage time among the country’s 10 most-used search and browser apps.
Google’s search app came fourth with 87 million hours, followed by Brave with 38 million hours and Daum with 23 million hours.
Whale recorded 5.7 million hours, while Nate and Firefox each logged 3.5 million hours. Microsoft Edge rounded out the top 10 with 1.8 million hours.

For brands and digital retailers in South Korea, the continued shift away from Naver’s integrated ecosystem toward Chrome reshapes consumer discovery pathways. Naver built its commercial engine by bundling search results directly with its own shopping comparison engine, smart stores, and payment rails. When shoppers conduct queries directly in a web browser rather than inside Naver’s walled garden, default search engine settings and standard web indexing dilute that proprietary checkout loop.

Google’s expanding footprint also splits consumer attention between dedicated mobile apps and direct web links. Retailers that previously focused technical resources exclusively on Naver SEO and proprietary storefronts now face higher ad spending requirements to capture high-intent buyers across multiple independent search feeds.

sum: SK hynix, the memory-chip and AI-server component supplier SKHY, presents another way to sell memory into AI infrastructure: shared capacity across servers. Its Korean shares closed at ?1,272,000, up 0.79% on October 16. The pitch goes beyond high-bandwidth memory. More types of memory inside each AI installation could give the company more products to sell.

In its October 16 disclosure, SK hynix described a 256-gigabyte CXL 3.2 module delivering 80 gigabytes per second of bandwidth, with roughly 30% better energy efficiency than its predecessor, according to the company. It also outlined proof-of-concept work with NAVER Cloud to share cached AI data. That is a technical milestone. It does not establish a volume order, a shipment schedule or a revenue contribution.

The GF Score of 76/100 shows strong growth, profitability and financial strength readings, alongside a sharply weaker momentum reading. That gives investors useful context, but it does not settle the commercial question. A successful demonstration still needs to turn into customer qualifications and paying orders. Shared memory could help customers squeeze more work from their servers; the payoff for SK hynix depends on how many modules they buy and the margins those sales deliver.

Kurly revisits IPO as profits improve, Naver backing grows
sum: Online grocery platform continues talks with underwriters, but valuation concerns and listing timeline remain uncertain

Online Korean grocery platform Kurly is reviving plans for an initial public offering as improving profitability and a partnership with Naver strengthen its valuation prospects, potentially opening an exit route for long-standing investors.

According to market sources Wednesday, Kurly has been holding regular discussions with its IPO underwriters — Korea Investment & Securities, NH Investment & Securities and JPMorgan — over a possible listing.
"We continue to hold regular meetings with our underwriters, but our focus remains on improving performance and enhancing our valuation," a Kurly official said.

The renewed IPO prospects follow a turnaround in earnings. Kurly posted revenue of 2.37 trillion won ($1.7 billion) and operating profit of 13.1 billion won last year, achieving its first annual operating profit since its founding.

Momentum has continued this year. In the first half, the company recorded revenue of 1.08 trillion won, operating profit of 51.6 billion won and net profit of 45.7 billion won. Its six-month operating profit was nearly four times its full-year figure for 2025, while it also swung to a net profit.

Kurly previously pursued an IPO after securing a valuation of around 4 trillion won in a 2021 pre-IPO funding round, but shelved the plan in 2023 amid deteriorating market conditions and a declining valuation.

Naver Z workers strike to oppose wage freeze, press CEO Kim Chang-uk
sum: The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU) Korean Chemical, Textile & Food Workers' Union (KCTFU) Naver chapter said Naver Z union members began a one-day all-out strike on the 23rd. Naver Z is the operator of the Metaverse platform "Zepeto."

According to the union, about 120 Naver Z members, or roughly 70%, are taking part in the all-out strike that day. The union said members plan to join a YouTube live stream from 10 a.m. for 30 minutes and argue that management is shifting responsibility for worsening business conditions onto employees by freezing wages.

The union also held a four-hour partial strike on the 9th to urge management to take a more forward-leaning stance in the 2026 wage negotiations. At the time, the union demanded the withdrawal of the unilateral wage freeze, a 5.3% wage increase, and a responsible explanation from Naver Z CEO Kim Chang-uk about the business situation. However, the union said that in the two weeks after the partial strike, management provided no response to the demands for a wage increase and an explanation from executives.

The union specifically claimed that after CEO Kim Chang-uk took sole charge of the Zepeto service, companywide town hall meetings were held only twice, in April 2024 and February 2025. Accordingly, the union argued that management froze wages citing a management crisis without sufficiently explaining the service's direction and vision or communicating with employees. Kim concurrently serves as co-CEO of four key Naver subsidiaries and affiliates: Snow, Naver Z, Kream, and Cake. Among them, Naver Z and Cake have frozen employee annual salaries this year.

Oh Se-yun, head of the Naver chapter, said, "A culture of wielding authority without taking responsibility keeps repeating at Naver," adding, "In normal times they do not share authority with employees, and when the company struggles, they shift the cause and responsibility onto employees." He continued, "Our demand to withdraw the salary freeze and hold a decisive debate with CEO Kim Chang-uk on Jet's future still stands," adding, "After the Chuseok holiday ends, we will send an open inquiry to CEO Kim Chang-uk and Chair Lee Hae-jin."

sum: NAVER and NVIDIA’s gigawatt (GW)-scale AI factory agreement, announced last June, took concrete shape through two contracts signed in July. On July 22, NAVER signed a preliminary agreement worth $9 billion with global investment firm Brookfield, and on the 24th, signed a strategic investment agreement worth $1 billion with NVIDIA. That same afternoon, at the AI Summit in San Francisco, NAVER Board Chairman Lee Hae-jin shared the background and significance of this partnership.

As global demand for AI surges, competition to secure the large-scale computing resources needed for AI model development and service operation – so-called “AI factories” – is intensifying. An AI factory is a new form of AI infrastructure that combines GPU computing resources with networking, storage, power and cooling systems, and software platforms into a single unit.

NAVER recognized the value of data centers early on and has continued to invest aggressively. It became the first Korean IT company to build its own self-designed data centers – “GAK Chuncheon” (2013) and “GAK Sejong” (2023) – and has directly operated every layer of the AI factory stack, from data centers and GPU clusters to AI platforms, its own models, and services.

NAVER is the only company in Korea that provides large-scale GPUaaS (GPU-as-a-Service), and is recognized as one of the few companies in the world capable of leading a sovereign AI business. For NAVER, this partnership will be a decisive opportunity to expand that capability onto the global stage.
Backed by NVIDIA’s $1 billion strategic investment and $9 billion in AI infrastructure assets to be raised by Brookfield, NAVER will build a $10 billion AI factory.

The AI factory will run on NVIDIA’s optimized platform, the “DSX Architecture,” with the latest Blackwell GPU platform and the next-generation Vera Rubin platform to be introduced in phases. Once the definitive agreement with the preferred bidder is signed, Brookfield will raise up to $9 billion through a special purpose vehicle (SPV) to fund the capital and infrastructure needed to build the AI factory.

To further strengthen this partnership, NVIDIA has decided to participate in NAVER’s third-party private placement of new shares worth approximately $1 billion – the first such investment by NVIDIA in Asia.

sum: Naver is strengthening its dominance in South Korea’s search market as its conversational AI search service gains traction, highlighting how AI-powered tools are reshaping the way users discover information, shop and make reservations online.

According to market research firm InternetTrend and Naver on Sunday, the company’s average search market share rose to 66.34 percent between April 27 and June 17, following the launch of its AI Tab beta service. That compares with an average share of 63.82 percent between Jan. 1 and April 26, before the service was introduced.
The increase suggests that Naver’s push into generative AI is helping attract users in an increasingly competitive search environment.
The company recorded a search market share of 81.34 percent on May 24, while its share exceeded 70 percent on multiple occasions after the beta launch.

AI Tab combines Naver’s search infrastructure with artificial intelligence and the company’s shopping and local business services. Users can interact with the service through natural language conversations, receiving information as well as recommendations that can lead directly to reservations, purchases and other actions.

Unlike Naver’s existing AI Briefing feature, which summarizes search results, AI Tab is designed as a more agent-like service that supports follow-up questions, deeper exploration and transaction-based activities.

Industry observers say the rise of generative AI may actually be reinforcing Naver’s position in search. Many users first obtain general answers from services such as ChatGPT or Gemini before turning to Naver for local information, shopping research and place-related searches.

AI Briefing is also cited as a pillar of stronger search competitiveness. AI Briefing quickly analyzes and summarizes multiple documents to provide key information. Naver plans to keep expanding AI Briefing coverage to about 40% of all search queries by year-end.

◇ ETFs are packed with Samsung and Hynix… Similar-theme competition stirs controversy

First, the ETF market's concentration in "Samjeon-nix" is steepening. Of the 49 new ETFs listed this year, 14 (29%) have Samsung Electronics and SK hynix as core assets. Products are pouring out to ride the semiconductor duo's soaring share prices. On the 22nd, even single-stock leveraged ETFs that track each of the two stocks at 2 times are slated to debut. The heat is intense, with 10,000 people signing up in a week just for the pre-education required to trade the products.

But the overheated product race is creating side effects of market distortion. Shinhan Asset Management promoted that it raised SK hynix exposure to 40% when launching "SOL AI Semiconductor TOP2 Plus," but the actual inclusion weight was only 24%. After criticism that it caused an "optical illusion" by adding in the weight of the holding company SK Square, the company belatedly corrected the figures and bowed its head.
◇ The semiconductor top two diverged a year ago… Now, "everyone" buys both

The structure of foreign inflows is also changing. In the past, foreign funds were spread across various industries beyond semiconductors, but recently they have been concentrating on Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.

As recently as a year ago, fortunes diverged between Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. In May last year, SK hynix ranked No. 1 in net foreign buying, while Samsung Electronics was No. 1 in net foreign selling. The gap in high-bandwidth memory (HBM) competitiveness within Nvidia's supply chain had an impact. SK hynix was the first in the industry to supply HBM3E 8‑stack and 12‑stack products, lifting market expectations, while Samsung Electronics at the time had not passed Nvidia's quality test.

South Korean probe tests U.S. willingness to protect its tech giants abroad
sum: South Korea wants to punish its biggest online retailer for a massive data leak. The U.S. is stepping in to shield Coupang, because even though it operates almost entirely in South Korea, it is registered as an American company.

Since last November, Coupang has been under fire after South Korean regulators found a former employee used a stolen security key to access personal information from 33.7 million accounts, about two-thirds of the population, over months without anyone noticing. South Korea’s science ministry called it a management failure, and regulators have opened separate investigations into algorithm rigging and unfair business practices.

Fifty-four Republican lawmakers wrote to South Korea’s ambassador on April 20, accusing the country of a “whole-of-government assault” on Coupang after the data breach. The letter accused South Korea of unfairly raiding Coupang’s offices, imposing fines and tax audits, threatening to revoke its business license, and pressuring South Korean public pension funds to dump their Coupang holdings.

The dispute underscores a bigger question about who gets to regulate a company that dominates one country’s market while registered under another’s laws. For the U.S., the ability to shield Coupang — a New York Stock Exchange-listed company with significant American backing — signals how well it can protect its business interests on foreign soil.

“The U.S. government and Congress are mandated to protect U.S. companies, and advance our interests overseas, so it is logical and normal that the executive and legislative branch are weighing in to support Coupang, and also U.S. business interests in Korea more broadly,” Henry Haggard, senior adviser at WestExec Advisors and former minister counselor at the U.S. Embassy in Seoul, told Rest of World.

Ninety-six South Korean lawmakers fired back in a letter to the U.S. ambassador on April 28, saying “the investigation and adjudication of alleged criminal conduct are the exclusive authority of a sovereign state.”
Greenoaks and Altimeter Capital, two of Coupang’s U.S. investors, sued the South Korean government in January, alleging the investigation was discriminatory.

Naver’s Search Market Share Hits 64% While Google Ranked 2nd with 29% Share
sum: Naver’s strong market share is due to the advancement of its artificial intelligence-based search services while Google ranked second with an average share of 28.7%
Naver’s search market share has maintained a strong position in the 60 percent range this year, continuing its dominance in the domestic search market.

According to market research firm InternetTrend on April 16, Naver’s average monthly search share stood at 65.1 percent in February and 63.8 percent in March. Notably, it exceeded 70 percent on specific days, reaching 70.6 percent on Feb. 28 and 70.4 percent on March 1.

During the same period, Google ranked second with a monthly average share of 28.7 percent in March. Microsoft’s search engine Bing and Daum followed in third and fourth place with 3.9 percent and 3.1 percent, respectively. Other search services, such as Zum and Yahoo, failed to reach a 1 percent share.

Industry observers attribute Naver’s strong market share to the advancement of its artificial intelligence-based search services. Following the introduction of its AI Briefing service last year, the company has enhanced both search convenience and accuracy in areas requiring high reliability by launching specialized search functions for health, public sectors, and securities.

Some analysts say the spread of generative AI has, in fact, stimulated demand for Naver search. Demand for cross-verification is increasing, as users first obtain general information through generative AI and then return to portals like Naver to confirm the latest updates and more detailed content, leading to increased reuse of Naver search.

The domestic specialized content ecosystem is also regarded as a structural strength for Naver. The company’s accumulation of locally relevant information across areas such as shopping, finance and health, along with content reflecting South Korea’s social and cultural context, continues to attract users in ways that are difficult for global search engines or overseas AI services to replicate.

sum: Dunamu reported a decline in earnings last year and postponed its planned share swap with NAVER Financial by about three months.

The company said Monday in a regulatory filing that its 2025 consolidated revenue fell 10.0% year-on-year to 1.5578 trillion won. Operating profit declined 26.7% to 869.3 billion won, while net profit dropped 27.9% to 708.9 billion won.

Dunamu attributed the decline to reduced trading volumes amid a global economic slowdown. About 98.26% of its revenue is generated from transaction fees on platforms such as Upbit. Fee revenue totaled 1.5307 trillion won in 2025, compared with 1.7094 trillion won in 2024.

Previously, Dunamu decided in June 2025 to spin off its Securities Plus Unlisted business unit. In September, it sold a 70% stake in the unit to NAVER Financial, and in November agreed to a comprehensive share swap with the company.

Dunamu also revised its schedule, setting the shareholder meeting for Aug. 18, 2026, and the share swap date for Sept. 30, 2026, delaying the timeline by about three months from the original late-June plan. The company said the transaction requires regulatory approvals, including antitrust clearance from the Fair Trade Commission, approval for a change in major shareholder of NAVER Financial, and acceptance of a major shareholder change filing for Dunamu.
It added that the schedule could face further delays or the deal could be canceled depending on the progress of relevant regulatory processes.
"We are currently proceeding with government approval procedures, and Dunamu and NAVER Financial are following the relevant regulatory processes step by step," the company said.

sum: "It seems management isn't interested in boosting the stock price."
"I'm stuck with a 30% loss, and the stock still isn't rising. It's frustrating."
"Instead of raising the cap on directors' compensation, freeze it and increase shareholder dividends first."

At Naver's 2026 shareholders meeting held on the 23rd at the Naver Green Factory in Bundang-gu, Seongnam, Gyeonggi, shareholders kept up sharp demands. Despite record earnings and increased dividends, the stock price has struggled to gain momentum, leading shareholders to ask the company to present plans to enhance shareholder value before expanding investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and new businesses. Naver's share price has fallen 30.5% from the June high last year of 298,000 won to 207,000 won on the 9th of this month.

Naver posted record results last year with sales of 12.035 trillion won and operating profit of 2.2081 trillion won on a consolidation basis. The settlement of account dividends also increased from 1,130 won to 2,630 won per share, and the total dividends rose from 168.4 billion won to 393.6 billion won. Still, shareholders cited the sluggish stock rebound despite the earnings improvement and dividends expansion, saying their perceived satisfaction was not high.

Naver CEO Choi Soo-yeon said that day, "We will expand our mid- to long-term growth foundation based on AI- and data-driven platform competitiveness, new technologies, and global business." Naver said it expanded the Generative AI-based integrated search result summary service "AI Briefing" to about 20% of integrated search queries last year, with about 30 million users. Search platform sales were 4.1689 trillion won, up 5.6% from a year earlier, and commerce sales were 3.6884 trillion won, up 26.2%.

Naver also unveiled a plan to comprehensively upgrade its service structure around AI this year. Starting with the recently introduced shopping agent, it will sequentially roll out vertical AI agents in local (maps and places), finance, and health, and it plans to expand advertising into external media and out-of-home ads by advancing AI solutions such as AD Boost.

items.t: Soop pivots to esports to counter Chzzk surge and remake Korea image
sum: As Naver's streaming platform "CHZZK" rapidly attracts users, SOOP (formerly AfreecaTV) is moving to restructure by putting e-sports at the forefront. It is an attempt to redefine itself as a pro sports–based content platform, moving away from a revenue model centered on individual channels designed to elicit large paid donations—such as "accel" streams—built on paid support (Star Balloons). However, analysts say it remains to be seen whether the image shift will translate into real results, as the existing revenue structure is still in place.

According to app analytics platform Mobile Index on the 22nd, Naver CHZZK's monthly active users (MAU) totaled 3,548,705 as of last month. By contrast, SOOP stayed at about 2,300,029 over the same period.

While CHZZK has grown its MAU to the mid-3 million range in just over two years since its launch at the end of 2023, SOOP has seen its MAU gradually decline from about 3 million in 2021 to the low-2 million range. With the overall domestic streaming market at about 5 million, observers say user movement is concentrating on CHZZK.

However, SOOP still holds an edge in real-time engagement metrics. As of the 18th, based on Softcon viewership streaming data, SOOP's average concurrent viewers were about 60,000, outpacing CHZZK (about 37,000). It trails in user scale, but maintains strengths in time spent and loyalty among heavy users.

In this environment, SOOP's answer is e-sports. The company changed its name to SOOP in 2024, declared a shift to a mass, global platform, and put e-sports front and center as a core pillar. The strategy aligns with shedding its past image.

SOOP has long faced criticism for its Star Balloon–based revenue structure and some suggestive programming. In particular, some channels combined tactics that encouraged large donations with content centered on female BJs, fostering competitive donation behavior among users, which has been cited as the backdrop for this image. Even now, the top Star Balloon donor rankings are dominated by individual channel content, and related controversies have not been fully resolved.
The most symbolic recent change at SOOP is its investment in broadcast rights for the LCK (League of Legends Champions Korea).

items.t: Search built Naver. Now AI commerce may define its future
sum: As AI tools take over knowledge searches, Naver turns shopping into its next gateway
Type “sofa” into Naver’s shopping app these days, and something different happens.

Instead of a grid of product listings, an AI agent asks questions. Do you live alone? Do you have pets? It notices browsing patterns suggesting a dog in the household and recommends waterproof fabrics and scratch-resistant materials. Then it proposes a specific product: a three-seat Aquatex sofa from Carrem Furniture, discounted 41 percent to 347,000 won ($235), rated 4.74 stars.
Ask it to compare brands, and it instantly generates a specification table.

This is Naver’s Shopping AI Agent 1.0 that launched in beta last week. On the surface, it looks like another AI feature. But it highlights a larger question playing out in one of the few markets where Google never fully took over: Can a local platform use its ecosystem to stay competitive in the age of generative search?

Globally, South Korea’s internet landscape has long been an anomaly. Naver’s search share once reached 78 percent in 2015. While that dominance has eroded, it remained strong at roughly 62 percent in 2025, according to government data.

When generative AI tools like ChatGPT emerged in late 2022, many analysts predicted the position would quickly weaken. Instead, Naver has continued posting record financial results — largely because search stopped being its core business years ago.

items.t: Naver launches open beta of new social media platform in North America
sum: Naver launched the open beta of its new user-generated content (UGC) platform, ThingsBook on Monday (local time), targeting the North American market.

ThingsBook is a text-based social platform for users to create personal collections that thoughtfully document their experiences with movies, books, music, travel destinations and daily life while connecting and communicating with others who share similar interests.

The platform also offers an advanced editor that allows users to enrich their text-based posts with images, locations, ratings and links, helping them better express their experiences and perspectives.

“Naver has consistently ventured into overseas markets with global strategies tailored to local cultures and user characteristics. With ThingsBook as well, we aim to establish it as a platform that works closely with local users to build a creative culture centered on records and personal taste,” Kim Seung-eon, Naver’s global community business leader, said.
“Through this global challenge, we will continue to raise the level of the service to help build a meaningful content ecosystem and community culture suited for the artificial intelligence (AI) era.”

ThingsBook uses an archival structure where personal preferences are organized into curated collections rather than in a typical chronological feed structure, enabling users to manage their records systematically.

Naver ran a closed beta for three months starting last October, closely monitoring usage patterns and needs of North American users. Based on extensive feedback collected during that period, the company improved service stability and key functions, and aims to further enhance the platform with a broader user base from the open beta.

items.t: Naver expands luxury reach as Chanel Beauty opens store on Highend in Korea

Naver touted a high online shopping experience by offering the product selection sold on Chanel's official mall along with visually focused brand content.

Customers can join Chanel's integrated membership "Chanel Code" to enjoy the same membership benefits, and Chanel products purchased at Naver's brand store come with free shipping. By bringing seasonal limited editions and bestsellers together in one place and highlighting gift wrapping, the companies are targeting online VIP demand. Another feature is strengthening authenticity trust through the operation of the official brand store.

Since 2020, Naver has strengthened its luxury category, with a particular focus on expanding its luxury beauty competitiveness. items.t: AI leaders Naver, Kakao struggle despite KOSPI's record-breaking rally
sum: Naver and Kakao, once hailed as the country’s flagship IT blue chips and leading artificial intelligence (AI) players, have largely failed to join the recent KOSPI rally, even as the benchmark index has continued to climb and fuel optimism it could hit 5,000 points.

According to the Korea Exchange Monday, Kakao’s shares fell 4.7 percent from the start of 2026 through last Friday, while Naver posted a gain of just over 1 percent, sharply underperforming compared to the broader market. KOSPI closed above the 4,800 level on Friday to set fresh record highs.

Data from NH Investment and Securities showed that nearly 90 percent of Kakao investors are currently in the red, with an average return of minus 29.57 percent. Naver is little better off, with 75.3 percent of its investors sitting on losses and an average return of minus 9.38 percent.
Kakao’s stock hit an all-time high of 173,000 won ($117) on June 24, 2021, during the market surge at the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, but has trended downward ever since.

Naver, meanwhile, surged to around 300,000 won last June following the launch of the Lee Jae Myung administration and the appointment of former Naver executive Ha Jung-woo as senior presidential secretary for AI and future planning. After months of volatile trading, however, the stock is now trading about 15 percent below that peak.
Market analysts said Naver and Kakao’s long-standing image as the main pillars of the government-led sovereign AI project has, paradoxically, weighed on their share prices.

Investor sentiment deteriorated sharply after both companies said they would not return to the competition, overseen by the Ministry of Science and ICT, to build sovereign AI foundation models after being dropped from the race. The disappointment was particularly pronounced in Naver’s case, as the IT giant had been widely viewed as a strong contender.

items.t: Poshmark Responds To Seller Backlash With New Updates, Pledges Greater Transparency In 2026
sum: Poshmark has responded to recent seller discontent with new updates and promises of improved transparency and communication about where the company is going under new leadership in 2026.

As CEO Manish Chandra and other executives left the company in the back half of 2025, with Korean parent company Naver taking a more active role in steering policy and product development at Poshmark, sellers have been on a roller coaster ride with the platform.

From controversial changes like the Excessive Listing Removal policy, feed visibility and discovery, killing off and then reintroducing bulk sharing, new cancellation policies, and Poshmark beginning to compete directly against sellers by hosting their own live Posh Shows, seller complaints about lack of transparency and communication have reached a fevered pitch in recent months.

But now the company is trying to win back some goodwill by introducing in app "Posh Previews" providing quarterly insights into priorities and changes for the platform as well as a new blog post with more details about recent seller updates.
For the first quarterly preview, Poshmark highlighted work they are doing to help the right buyers find the right listings and build trust in the platform.

As we step into a new year, we want to start with a sincere thank you. Your dedication helped make 2025 our strongest holiday season yet. We know Poshmark has evolved over the past year, and we’re excited to keep building together in 2026.

Today, we’re introducing Posh Preview, a quarterly update designed to give you more transparency into Poshmark’s priorities. At the start of each quarter, you’ll get a look at what we’re working on and have the opportunity to share feedback to help shape what’s next.

sum: Korea's webtoon industry continued its strong growth momentum in 2024, with total annual revenue exceeding 2 trillion won ($1.397 billion) for the second consecutive year, government data showed Monday.

The domestic webtoon market generated an estimated 2.286 trillion won in revenue in 2024, up 4.4 percent from 2.189 trillion won a year earlier, according to the 2025 industry survey report released by the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism and its affiliate, the Korea Creative Content Agency.

The report showed the sector has expanded steadily since 2018, when the government began compiling official statistics. Webtoon revenue stood at just 379.9 billion won in 2017 but surged past the 1 trillion won mark in 2020 and topped 2 trillion won for the first time in 2023.

Japan remained the largest overseas market for Korean webtoons, accounting for 49.5 percent of total exports, followed by North America at 21 percent, Chinese-speaking regions at 13 percent, Southeast Asia at 9.5 percent and Europe at 6.2 percent. Online transmission rights accounted for 84 percent of total exports, while publishing rights and derivative work licenses made up smaller shares.

On the import side, Japan also held the largest share at 51.3 percent, followed by the Chinese-speaking market at 41.2 percent, Europe at 4.2 percent, North America at 2.3 percent and Southeast Asia at 0.9 percent. The report said online transmission rights accounted for the majority of imports, at 76 percent.

items.t: Naver Corporation and Dunamu Inc. ‘Big Deal’ Imminent... What Happened to the Companies Naver Once Acquired?
sum: A merger between Naver Corporation, a leading big tech company in South Korea, and Dunamu Inc., operator of the cryptocurrency exchange Upbit, is imminent. This alliance goes beyond a simple business partnership. By building a financial ecosystem and expanding global services, it is expected to reshape the fintech landscape.

According to the IT industry on the 26th, Naver Corporation and NAVER Financial Corporation are holding board meetings today to approve a merger plan that will make Dunamu Inc. a subsidiary of NAVER Financial Corporation. Dunamu Inc. is also following suit. During these meetings, Lee Hae-jin, Chairman of the Board at Naver Corporation, and Song Chi-hyung, Chairman of Dunamu Inc., are expected to explain the significance of the merger and outline post-merger plans.

The merger will be executed through a comprehensive stock swap. The likely exchange ratio is three shares of NAVER Financial Corporation for each share of Dunamu Inc. NAVER Financial Corporation will issue a large number of new shares. Once the share swap is completed, Song Chi-hyung, Vice Chairman Kim Hyung-nyeon, and other Dunamu Inc. executives will become the largest shareholders, holding a 29.5% stake. Naver Corporation's stake will be diluted from 69% to 17%.

Lee Hae-jin has consistently pursued various mergers and acquisitions (M&A) to enhance competitiveness in new business areas. Hangame Communication is a notable example. Hangame Communication, founded by Kim Beom-soo, the creator of Kakao, is an online gaming platform. Naver Corporation acquired Hangame Communication, which at the time was valued at 62.5 billion KRW. Back then, Naver Corporation was a startup established in 1999 with a capital of 500 million KRW and annual sales of 1.8 billion KRW.

In 2000, Naver Corporation merged with Hangame Communication, internet marketing solution company ONEQ, and search engine technology research firm Search Solution. The merger terms included issuing 2.59733 shares of Naver Corporation common stock for each share of Hangame, and 1.61333 shares for each share of ONEQ. For Search Solution, Naver Corporation exchanged 15% of its shares for 40% of Search Solution’s shares, making it an affiliate, and later acquired additional shares to make it a subsidiary.

sum: Deal marks Korea’s biggest fintech consolidation, expanding Naver’s reach into crypto, trading, tokenized finance

South Korea’s leading internet platform Naver and cryptocurrency exchange operator Dunamu are moving toward a landmark merger that would create a 20 trillion won ($13.6 billion) fintech powerhouse, combining payments, digital assets and artificial intelligence-driven financial services under one roof.

Naver said Wednesday that its board, along with that of its fintech affiliate Naver Financial, approved a sweeping share-swap agreement under which Naver Financial will acquire full ownership of Dunamu, the operator of Korea’s largest crypto exchange, Upbit.

Under the proposed terms, each Dunamu share will be exchanged for 2.54 shares of Naver Financial. The ratio implies a valuation of roughly 15 trillion won for Dunamu and about 5 trillion won for Naver Financial. A shareholder vote is set for May 22, with the transaction scheduled to close by June 30 if approved.

Once completed, the deal would mark one of the most consequential consolidations in Korea’s fintech and virtual asset sectors, uniting Naver’s vast digital ecosystem with Dunamu’s blockchain infrastructure and deep liquidity in crypto markets.

Naver founder Lee Hae-jin and Dunamu Chair Song Chi-hyung are slated to hold a rare joint press conference Thursday to detail their strategic roadmap. The event marks Lee’s first public appearance in nearly nine years, signaling the weight the company places on the merger.

“The integration of Dunamu will enable us to create powerful synergies across AI, search, digital payments and blockchain technology,” a Naver official said. “As global tech shifts toward a Web3 paradigm, this merger positions us at the forefront of innovation and international expansion.”

items.t: Naver, Dunamu near merger to form 20 tn won fintech giant
sum: Naver Financial, operator of Korea’s leading payment service Naver Pay, and Dunamu, the company behind the nation’s largest cryptocurrency exchange Upbit, are nearing a merger that could create a 20 trillion won ($14.7 billion) fintech powerhouse.
According to industry sources on Wednesday, the two companies plan to hold board meetings around Nov. 26 to vote on a comprehensive stock swap proposal.

The two sides have tentatively agreed on a share exchange ratio of one Dunamu share for three Naver Financial shares, based on valuations of about 15 trillion won for Dunamu and 5 trillion won for Naver Financial.

If finalized, Dunamu Chairman Song Chi-hyung and other executives will become the largest shareholders of the merged entity, holding roughly 28 percent, while Naver — which currently owns 70 percent of Naver Financial — will see its stake diluted to around 17 percent, becoming the second-largest shareholder.

However, Naver has reportedly reached an agreement to secure more than half of the merged company’s voting rights from Dunamu’s management to meet Korea’s Fair Trade Act requirement for “substantial control.” This would allow Naver to consolidate Dunamu’s annual operating profit — estimated at over 1 trillion won — into its financial statements, while Dunamu gains institutional legitimacy by aligning with a major tech group.

A key remaining issue is winning over existing Dunamu shareholders. A senior company official said, “We are working to convene the board next week. While shareholders’ positions differ, we are coordinating to reach a majority consensus.”

Some major investors are raising concerns over valuation fairness. Mirae Asset Securities, which holds a 30 percent stake in Naver Financial, reportedly supports the merger in principle but believes the valuation favors Dunamu.

items.t: Spotify tops 700 mil. users after price hike, accelerates expansion in Korea
sum: Spotify secured a significant milestone this quarter, reaching a total of 700 million monthly active users (MAUs) even after raising subscription prices in key global markets.

The company reported quarterly revenue of 4.27 billion euros ($4.9 billion), a 7 percent rise from the same period last year, with operating profit reaching 582 million euros, reflecting a 43 percent surge. Its net income turned positive from the previous quarter’s loss, hitting 899 million euros.
The jump in users was driven both by the subscription fee increase and a successful global marketing push, with signups outpacing the company’s expectations.

The increased subscription fees have contributed to boosting its revenue. In August, Spotify raised its monthly premium subscription price from 10.99 euros ($12.63) to 11.99 euros across major markets, including Europe, Asia-Pacific, Africa and the Middle East.

The streaming service has been expanding its business, recently pinpointing video content and video podcasts as future growth areas. In just the third quarter, it rolled out 30 major feature updates, including artificial intelligence (AI)-powered content recommendations, playlist mixing tools and an in-app direct messaging service.
Last month, the company signed a deal to provide its video podcast content and other video features to Netflix.
Spotify has also been putting effort into expanding its presence in Korea's music streaming market.
